items.name: AI shell suggestions can execute before the user presses Enter
items.priority: F01 Critical · Reproduced · remains in reviewed main
items.current_evidence: Shell suggestions reject C0/DEL/C1 before cleaning and remain in read-only review. Copy is the only transfer action; there is no insertion into an arbitrary PTY.
items.required_change: Recommended change. Reject terminal control characters, including CR, LF, ESC, NUL and C1 controls, in shell suggestions. Keep the result in a read-only review view until an explicit Insert action. Insert only into a verified idle shell prompt; never into an arbitrary foreground program or partially typed command. Treat bracketed paste as transport, not as an execution authorization boundary.
items.acceptance: Acceptance. A synthetic hostile response cannot create a marker or alter terminal state in shells with bracketed paste on/off; ESC terminators and control-byte variants are rejected. Ordinary safe suggestions remain reviewable and require a separate user submission.
items.baseline_evidence: The “Ask AI for a shell command” workflow promises to type a suggestion without running it. A lone carriage return embedded inside the returned string survives cleaning. With a visible /bin/sh session, the string is written directly to the PTY and the carriage return submits it.
acceptance_criteria: Control-byte variants cannot execute or alter PTY state; safe suggestions require manual paste and separate shell submission.
items.verification_scope: Source/module/protocol and recorded native PTY evidence as applicable; packaged exact-commit gates recorded separately.

items.name: Released Claude transport forwards the key through redirects
items.priority: F02 High · Reproduced in 0.3.0 · fixed in source, awaiting released verification
items.current_evidence: Retains PR #9 no-redirect/redacted Debug protections and applies them to cancellable streaming. Official 0.3.0 RED forwards a dummy key; candidate PTY target receives zero requests.
items.required_change: Recommended change. Publish and verify a patched release containing PR #9, with an explicit upgrade note. Run the redirect regression against the packaged executable. Keep model/provider tests independent of real credentials.
items.acceptance: Acceptance. Redirect targets receive zero key-bearing requests; config Debug output contains no key; all distributed install paths resolve to the patched version.
remaining_gates: Publishing/upgrading latest release and distribution install paths requires explicit user authorization; latest 0.3.0 remains vulnerable until publication.
items.baseline_evidence: The downloaded release follows redirects. Its Claude adapter sends x-api-key, which can reach a different destination. Main disables redirects and redacts the configuration Debug representation, but users installing the latest published release still receive the older transport.
acceptance_criteria: No redirected credential-bearing request; upgrade distributed install paths only through an explicitly authorized patched release.
items.verification_scope: Source/module/protocol and recorded native PTY evidence as applicable; packaged exact-commit gates recorded separately.

items.name: Save replaces file identity without preserving all metadata
items.priority: F03 High · Reproduced xattr loss and hard-link divergence
items.current_evidence: Atomic save preserves supported xattrs, native ACL, owner/group/mode or refuses. Hard links are refused with independent Save As. Exclusive Save As, inode-bound conflict baseline and no-follow in-place fallback protect competing paths.
items.required_change: Recommended change. Define a save policy for hard links, ownership, ACLs and xattrs. Preserve supported metadata, detect unsupported cases and explain the tradeoff before proceeding. Do not silently switch every save to in-place writing: that introduces partial-write risks.
items.acceptance: Acceptance. Test user xattrs, group ownership, ACLs, hard links, symlinks, bind mounts and concurrent writers on claimed platforms. Either preserve the chosen contract or ask the user before a known destructive metadata transition.
tests: Actual extracted Linux musl POSIX ACL preservation and cross-owner refusal PTY (retained probe/log)
remaining_gates: Mounted VirtioFS does not support user xattrs; normal Linux filesystem xattrs verified. Safe save does not serialize uncooperative writers across final conflict-check/rename; exact claimed-platform results remain separate.
items.baseline_evidence: Atomic replacement creates a new inode and copies permission bits. It does not preserve user extended attributes or the original hard-link relationship. Owner/group and ACL preservation are also not implemented explicitly; those effects were not reproduced here. This is already acknowledged broadly in the FAQ, but matters particularly for an SSH/configuration editor.
acceptance_criteria: Native metadata fixtures survive atomic save; linked names and concurrent-writer fixtures retain existing work. Actual Linux EBUSY mount uses verified in-place policy.
items.verification_scope: Source/module/protocol and recorded native PTY evidence as applicable; packaged exact-commit gates recorded separately.

items.name: Formatter execution freezes the editor and can outlive its timeout
items.priority: F04 High · Reproduced · remains in reviewed main
items.current_evidence: Formatter workers bind identity/revision and cancellation; one bounded deadline covers stdin, process exit and inherited output pipes; process groups are terminated.
items.required_change: Recommended change. Move formatting off the UI thread with progress and cancellation. Bind the result to the original buffer identity/revision. Apply one deadline to process exit, input and output draining; bound output and terminate the formatter process group when cancelled/timed out.
items.acceptance: Acceptance. Typing, Escape and palette navigation respond during formatting. Hung descendants cannot outlive the operation deadline. Late output cannot overwrite edits made while formatting.
remaining_gates: One later local extracted macOS run had unexplained three-second marker timeouts; subsequent same-binary full24/isolated/controlled-load runs passed. Diagnostics added; no timeout weakening or unsupported root-cause claim.
items.baseline_evidence: Format-on-save calls a blocking process runner from the UI path. The runner has a 10-second child wait deadline, then joins pipe-reader threads after the direct child exits. A descendant that retains stdout/stderr can keep those joins blocked after the deadline.
acceptance_criteria: Palette stays interactive during formatter execution; stale output never edits; inherited pipes and descendants stop at deadline.
items.verification_scope: Source/module/protocol and recorded native PTY evidence as applicable; packaged exact-commit gates recorded separately.

items.name: Terminal paste silently ignores additional cursors
items.priority: F05 Medium · Reproduced · remains in reviewed main
items.current_evidence: Keyboard insertion, clipboard and bracketed paste share selection/multi-cursor/rectangle edit operations with grouped undo and grapheme boundaries. Clipboard workers reject stale selections.
items.required_change: Recommended change. Route bracketed paste and clipboard Paste through a shared edit operation, retaining the existing selection, multi-cursor and rectangle rules. Specify how multiline paste is distributed.
items.acceptance: Acceptance. Typing and each paste transport produce the expected edits at all active cursors; one undo restores the entire operation; test Unicode and rectangular selections too.
tests: Unicode multiple-cursor, clipboard, bracketed-paste and Alt+Shift rectangle PTY
items.baseline_evidence: The editor command for Paste supports extra cursors and rectangular selections. The bracketed terminal-paste event uses another path that updates only the ordinary selection or primary cursor. Common terminal paste gestures therefore behave differently from editor Paste.
acceptance_criteria: All transports produce exact expected Unicode bytes at each cursor/row; one undo/redo covers the entire edit.
items.verification_scope: Source/module/protocol and recorded native PTY evidence as applicable; packaged exact-commit gates recorded separately.

items.name: New indentation blocks always add four spaces
items.priority: F06 Medium · Reproduced · remains in reviewed main
items.current_evidence: Per-buffer width and style use content inference, supported .editorconfig settings and explicit status/palette overrides, shared by Enter, Tab/outdent and LSP formatting options.
items.required_change: Recommended change. Add per-buffer indentation width, content inference, .editorconfig support and an explicit status-bar override. Use that value consistently in insert, outdent, visual columns and formatter requests.
items.acceptance: Acceptance. Two-, four- and eight-space fixtures and tab-indented Makefiles retain their conventions across Enter, Tab, Outdent, paste and formatting.
items.baseline_evidence: The buffer detects tabs versus spaces, but the space indentation unit is hard-coded to four. There is no configurable width or .editorconfig integration in the reviewed settings. Preserving a current line’s indentation works; inferring the next block’s width does not.
acceptance_criteria: Two/four/eight-space fixtures and tab files retain conventions; explicit override is visible and persisted where configured. Supported editorconfig subset is documented.

items.name: Project search and discovery run synchronously while typing
items.priority: F08 Medium · Source-confirmed performance risk · not benchmarked over SSH
items.current_evidence: Debounced generation-tagged workers cancel and bound discovery/search; include/exclude scope and skipped/truncated results are visible; unsaved named buffers overlay disk.
items.required_change: Recommended change. Use a cancellable worker, a short debounce, query generations and incremental results. Show scope, skipped files and truncation. Add include/exclude filters and configurable limits; merge new unsaved buffers into discovery explicitly.
items.acceptance: Acceptance. A slow synthetic filesystem/search worker cannot stall typing or closing the panel. Old query results cannot replace a newer query. A cancelled query stops consuming resources.
remaining_gates: Slow-storage/SSH performance not measured; local synthetic cancellation/responsiveness evidence only.
items.baseline_evidence: Changing the project query calls search_project directly; it reads files on the event path. Initial discovery runs git ls-files with blocking output collection. The file/result limits bound much of the work, but do not make slow storage or process execution non-blocking.
acceptance_criteria: Slow synthetic workers do not block input; superseded results cannot publish; cancellation, scope and limit reporting are verified.
items.verification_scope: Source/module/protocol and recorded native PTY evidence as applicable; packaged exact-commit gates recorded separately.

items.name: Completion drops supporting edits such as imports
items.priority: F09 Medium · Source-confirmed missing LSP handling · live server impact untested
items.current_evidence: Completion resolve retains opaque provider data; primary/import edits validate and apply atomically. Unsupported completion commands are disclosed and never executed.
items.required_change: Recommended change. Support the advertised LSP completion contract or clearly constrain capabilities. Apply supporting text edits atomically with stale-document and overlap checks. Add completion-item resolution when requested by the server. Snippet support is a separate feature and currently advertised false.
items.acceptance: Acceptance. A fixture completion that inserts a symbol and adds an import applies both in one undo group. Stale or conflicting edits apply neither. Validate with at least one real Python and TypeScript server.
remaining_gates: Actual real-server stdio/core workflow verified; packaged interactive completion/import/navigation/Problems selection remains unqualified.
items.baseline_evidence: Completion parsing retains a label, insertion text and primary range. It does not retain additionalTextEdits or a completion command, and no completion-item resolve path was found. Some servers use those mechanisms to add imports or finish an edit.
acceptance_criteria: Real Python and TypeScript imports plus symbol insertion undo/redo together; stale, overlapping and malformed edits apply neither.
items.verification_scope: Source/module/protocol and recorded native PTY evidence as applicable; packaged exact-commit gates recorded separately.

items.name: Switching language families replaces the language-server process
items.current_evidence: Bounded workspace/server pool keeps language processes warm, synchronizes all open documents, aggregates file-named Problems and exposes restart/status. Interaction intents prevent abandoned navigation.
items.required_change: Recommended change. Pool clients by workspace and server identity. Keep all open documents synchronized and aggregate Problems across files with explicit scope. Bound idle servers and expose restart/status per language.
items.acceptance: Acceptance. Alternating two supported language families does not repeatedly start their servers. Unsaved open files retain diagnostics and references, and workspace Problems names each file.
tests: real mixed Pyright/TypeScript PID reuse, inactive unsaved diagnostics/references and workspace symbols
remaining_gates: Actual real-server stdio/core workflow verified; packaged interactive completion/import/navigation/Problems selection remains unqualified.
items.baseline_evidence: LanguageService owns one optional client. When the next document uses another server, it stops the current one and spawns the next. Same-server file switching is reused, which is good. Mixed Rust/Python/YAML/Terraform projects cannot keep each language service warm.
acceptance_criteria: Four alternating cycles preserve both server PIDs; inactive unsaved diagnostics/references retain correct file identity; closed/reopened requests do not revive.

items.name: Published archives lack a complete native artifact acceptance gate
items.priority: F12 Medium · Coverage gap · not a demonstrated broken package
items.current_evidence: Exact-SHA extracted-archive and package gates implemented for four native targets. Historical757 GitHub jobs passed ARM macOS and ARM/x64 Linux; owner switched to local Jenkins and cancelled unfinished Intel gate. Manual-only candidate workflow; automatic audit jobs allocate no Actions runners.
items.required_change: Recommended change. Run the existing PTY smoke suite against each extracted release archive on its native target. Add install/uninstall checks for .deb/.rpm and a documented Intel macOS gate, plus release provenance and signing/notarization work.
items.acceptance: Acceptance. Release evidence records the archive digest and exact executable under test for every claimed platform. Publication depends on the artifact gates, not only source tests and --version.
tests: scripts/test-artifact-provenance.sh: same-version stale-source and incorrect-target archives refused
All 24 PTY tests against extracted native macOS archive, Linux musl archive, installed deb and rpm; uninstall verified
Jenkins exact-SHA native gate with actual platform validation and always-archived evidence
remaining_gates: No local Intel macOS/native Linux agent is available; cancelled Intel job is not a passing native artifact result. Jenkins acceptance receipts identify the exact tested candidate SHA; check the linked build result and artifacts in PR11. Signing/notarization and publication remain separately blocked.
items.baseline_evidence: CI contains meaningful unit and PTY tests. However, tagged packaging builds separate musl/macOS target binaries and largely checks architecture and --version. The release publish job tests installer version output. The available archive-install PTY gate is not invoked by release.yml; Intel macOS is cross-built without a native Intel test in that workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Each claimed archive must pass all PTY tests on its native architecture with recorded source/archive/binary identity; no cross-build or unexecuted workflow substitutes for acceptance.
